svg.aria-label: CBCL architecture: participants hold sets of recorded speech acts that merge by union; acts cite predecessors; each candidate is checked against its dialect, producing unknown, valid or violation; admission yields an accepted subset A of received records S; state is derived from A by the dialect's fixed rules.

g.text: Interaction protocols over sets of recorded speech acts
Full recognition comes first; the numbered stages then run left to right.
Cards at the bottom are supporting concepts; captions carry the caveats.
Receiving c then a, or a then c,
not from the order records arrive.
Which predecessor acts must it cite?
all = least of the parts, any = greatest.
Unknown is a third value, not a failure;
it stays until evidence resolves it.
Passing one causal check alone does
Same accepted acts + same fixed rules
Recognition is distinct from causal validity, truthfulness and application safety.
recognised messages become records and enter step 1
then use D’s vocabulary in an explicit (lang D …) scope
The input message set is a deterministic context-free
language (DCFL). DCFLs are not closed under union in
general; CBCL’s prefix-free lang token makes each scoped
installation a deterministic union, so the set stays DCFL
after any finite sequence of installations.
These are responsibilities, not necessarily sequential processing stages.
CBCL relies on the other two but does not provide them.
a right is spent once, and
Set union alone does not prevent double spending.
Rights plus issuance or certification discipline constrain spending.
Rice’s theorem motivates the restriction; it does not supply the
preservation proof, and not every question about a DCFL is decidable.
Recorded speech acts become evidence for subsequent interactions.
Authentication establishes who said what — not that the statement is true.
